S4. MATERIAL FINDING 1: delayed post-commit stamp publication can overwrite a newer campaign synchronization or identity, defeating the durable discriminator. Authority: parent acceptance criteria 1 and 2 plus the USER ADJUSTMENT; ADR 0012:129-130, "a stale campaign database can never revert the timeline", and its no-silent-timeline-rewrite/continuity contract; ADR 0020 section 3 persistence/identity/ownership integrity; integrated design section 5.9 conditions 6 and 8. SRD page/quote: not applicable; this is Eshyra custody/persistence authority.

Mechanism: characterCustody.ts:372-384 unconditionally upserts BOTH global_character_id and synced_revision. The registry lock is already released when checkout (:200-209), sync (:469-478), release (:574-595), acquire (:845-892) and catch-up (:947-955) publish separate campaign stamps. A process paused after its actual registry COMMIT can later overwrite a stamp published by a newer completed operation on the SAME physical campaign database. BEGIN IMMEDIATE and the nesting guard do not cover that interval. readSyncedRevision (:366-368) treats an identity-mismatched row as legacy; isRestoredBehindHead (:402-410) rejects an original database with a regressed matching stamp once it has further unsynchronized progress.

Concrete two-process evidence: /tmp/pr711-current-review/postcommit-siblings.test.ts:69-112 and postcommit-worker.mts:11-23. The worker calls the actual atomically function, waits AFTER it commits and returns its unmodified result, then resumes the real custody helper. This models process preemption; it neither invents data nor bypasses a guard. For sync: A commits level 2 as revision 2 and pauses before stamping. B resumes the SAME original database, legitimately recovers the append-before-stamp interval, progresses to level 3, and completes revision/stamp 3. A then overwrites stamp 3 with stamp 2. B makes valid unsynchronized level-4 progress, closes and reopens the ORIGINAL path without restore/fork. It now classifies stale-copy at local 2/head 3; acquire throws, release returns undefined, and real CLI activation cancels through the stale-copy UX. Output: postcommit-sync-evidence.json. Valid original progress cannot resume/sync/release normally, violating acceptance criterion 2. Six passing reproducer cases show the same failure for sync, release, checkout, catch-up, already-held acquire and idle acquire, with postcommit-<mode>-evidence.json outputs.
S5. Same MATERIAL finding: identity/restore sibling and closure. /tmp/pr711-current-review/postcommit-identity.test.ts:71-115 demonstrates acceptance-criterion-1 failure through the real release and stale-copy fork APIs, with an actual Dolt checkpoint/restore.

A releases mira level 2 as revision 2 and pauses after COMMIT, before its stamp. B resumes that original database and stamps 2; another synchronized same-campaign copy advances/releases mira revision 3. B's older level-2 campaign is correctly classified stale-copy. Actual activateCampaignCustody fork choice creates fork-probe revision 1, attaches it into pc-1 and stamps fork-probe@1. A finishes its delayed release stamp and replaces this NEW identity's stamp with mira@2, while the sheet still identifies fork-probe. CheckpointStore checkpoints that database and restores it through real Dolt. The original fork progresses/releases revision 2 at level 3 and reacquires custody. The restored fork remains level 2 but its stamp names mira, so readSyncedRevision treats it as unstamped: classification returns already-held, and release appends fork-probe revision 3 at level 2, overwriting the newer level-3 head. Evidence: postcommit-identity-evidence.json, forkHistory [[1,2],[2,3],[3,2]], source mira history [[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]]. This is NOT an old legacy database or the authorized same-base-first-sync residual: the fork was created and stamped under migration 0054; a delayed operation destroyed its valid discriminator.

Applicability/reachability: separate Node/tsx processes and SQLite connections, overlapping operations on the same physical campaign DB, followed by normal restore. CLI accepts same-campaign same-slot resume as already-held; /quit uses releaseCharacterFromCampaign (playClose.ts:46-58), and the real conflict UX performs the explicit fork used here. No enclosing transaction, fabricated store result or raw corruption is needed. The false-stale-original case needs overlapping completions; head overwrite additionally needs an explicit fork while an old release completion is delayed and a later checkpoint restore. These conditions limit frequency, not the demonstrated consequence.

Owner: this PR's custody/campaign-stamp publication boundary. Required closure: a delayed completion must not regress a newer durable synced revision or overwrite a newer attachment's freshness identity. Bind/serialize or conditionally publish stamps against current campaign identity and already-published synchronization state across ALL stamping operations, preserving ordinary crash recovery and legitimate original progress. A same-identity max-revision rule alone does not close the identity-replacement sibling. Inventory :2434/:2446 must remain truthful about resulting concurrency behavior. Permanent evidence should be a GENERALIZED invariant over delayed completion versus newer synchronization/attachment, protecting valid original resume and refusal of stale restored identity. Exact level fixtures and multi-process /tmp barriers need not become permanent; a deterministic two-connection interleaving is proportionate. This is ONE material publication defect class with two consequences. Material repair requires fresh full review.
